Which schools, roads and nearby colleges matter to Eastpointe buyers?

Eastpointe Community Schools reaches most parcels. It was called East Detroit Public Schools until 2017 and runs one high school, one middle school and four elementary schools. South Lake Schools claims the southeastern corner, and its Koepsell Elementary stands inside Eastpointe's borders. Confirm the district for your parcel before listing, since boundaries shape what a family will pay.

Gratiot Avenue (M-3) runs through the city, with I-94 and I-696 close by, and 8 Mile Road (M-102) and 9 Mile Road carry cross-town traffic. Macomb Community College's South Campus is two miles north in Warren, and the Wayne County Community College District's Mary Ellen Stempfle University Center is across 8 Mile Road in Harper Woods.

Local life centers on John F. Kennedy Memorial Park, the Cruisin' Gratiot car celebration in June and the late-July Erin-Halfway Days festival. The American Power Boat Association is headquartered in the city, and the first Art Van furniture showroom opened on Gratiot in 1959.

When are Eastpointe property taxes due?

The City Treasurer collects for the city, Macomb County, Macomb Community College, the intermediate school district, the state education tax and both school districts. About 30,000 bills go out each year, and both school districts ask that 100 percent of school tax appear on the summer bill.

  • Summer taxes are due July 1 with a September 1 deadline. Pay it all by September 1, or pay half by then and the other half by December 1.
  • Winter taxes are due December 1 with a February 15 deadline.
  • A summer balance left after September 1 grows by 1 percent a month, with 2 percent more from February 16.
  • A winter balance left after February 15 carries a 3 percent charge.
  • From March 1, unpaid taxes go to the Macomb County Treasurer at One South Main Street in Mount Clemens, with added penalties.

Eligible owners can defer summer taxes to February 15 if household income is $40,000 or less and they are 62 or older, disabled, a qualifying veteran, a surviving spouse or blind. The deferment application is due by September 15. For a payoff figure, call the taxes line at 586-445-3661, option 6.

What paperwork does the Eastpointe assessor handle after a sale?

Eastpointe's Assessing Department explains the sequence in plain terms. The buyer signs the principal residence exemption form at closing if the house will be owner-occupied. The seller signs a request to rescind the exemption and files it with the assessor, which clears the seller's name from the homestead and lets the seller claim it on the next home.

Buyers owe the assessor a Property Transfer Affidavit, due 45 days after the transfer. Each late day costs $5, capped at $200. The taxable value is uncapped the year after a transfer, so the new owner's bill rises to match the assessed value, which the city sets at half of market value.

An owner who thinks the value is too high must appear in March, since that is the only month the Board of Review hears opinions of value. The July and December sessions deal with clerical errors, mutual mistakes of fact and poverty requests. A homeowner who loses can take the case to the Michigan Tax Tribunal by June 30.

What state transfer taxes apply to an Eastpointe sale?

On an Eastpointe sale the seller pays the state transfer tax, $3.75 on each $500 block of value (MCL 207.525). Macomb County adds a levy of its own under MCL 207.504. The county deed office at 586-469-7953 can tell you the current total, and the county treasurer collects it, with a 15-day deadline that starts when the deed is delivered.

MCL 207.526 exempts, among others, a deed that does nothing but straighten a boundary line and a land contract that has not yet passed legal title. A land contract buyer can still claim the principal residence exemption if the contract is recorded or recordable.

Frequently asked questions

Is there a pre-sale inspection for an Eastpointe house?

The city's published rules cover rental registration and vacant property registration, not a general pre-sale inspection. If the house is a rental, the certificate may pass to the buyer if the buyer registers within 14 days. Call the Building Department to confirm your property's status.

When are Eastpointe summer and winter taxes due?

Summer bills are issued July 1 with a September 1 deadline, and winter bills December 1 with a February 15 deadline. Whatever is unpaid on March 1 goes to the Macomb County Treasurer.

How do I remove my principal residence exemption after selling?

Sign a request to rescind the exemption and file it with the Eastpointe Assessing Department. That clears your name from the homestead so you can claim the exemption on your next home.

What does the buyer file after an Eastpointe closing?

A Property Transfer Affidavit, filed at the Assessor's Office. The closing agent usually supplies the form, but the buyer must file it, and a filing later than 45 days costs $5 per day up to $200.

Which district serves an Eastpointe address?

Eastpointe Community Schools covers most parcels, while the southeastern corner belongs to South Lake Schools. Look up your parcel before you list.

Which sale method fits a Bay City house?

Selling in Bay City means choosing between an open-market listing, a sale you run yourself, and a cash purchase from someone who accepts the property in its present condition. All three finish with a recorded deed and Michigan transfer tax, so the real decision is how much time, repair work and uncertainty you want to carry.

An older house near the river often needs the most thought. Many Bay City homes date from the lumber era, and a buyer using a mortgage will usually order an inspection that turns up wiring, roofing or foundation items. A cash buyer prices those in and skips the repair negotiation.

  • Listing: the broadest audience and the longest wait, with repair requests likely.
  • Owner-run sale: no listing commission, yet you handle contract and disclosures.
  • Cash purchase: a simpler closing, with the price tied to the house's condition.

What is Bay City like beyond the listing?

Bay City is the Bay County seat, set on the Saginaw River just upstream from Saginaw Bay, with about 10 square miles of land. West Bay City, on the river's west bank, was a separate city until it was annexed in 1905, and several bridges still link the two sides. The Center Avenue Historic District holds more than 250 buildings on the National Register, many of them lumber-boom houses, and Midland Street and Water Street (home to a large antique district) anchor the older commercial areas.

The job base is a mix of health care, schools and industry. The city's financial report lists McLaren Bay Region (about 1,880 employees), Bay City Public Schools (792), Bay County (589), S. C. Johnson and Son (450) and General Motors Powertrain (432) among the top employers, and Michigan Sugar is also based here. Highways include I-75, US 10, M-13 and M-25.

The river brings an advantage and a caution. Waterfront and historic-district houses draw a particular kind of buyer, while the region's humid continental climate means cold winters that expose weak roofs and old heating systems.

Which Bay City neighborhoods and schools shape buyer interest?

Bay City Public Schools runs three high schools, Central, Western and Eastern, along with two middle schools and seven elementary schools, so a house's attendance zone is a real selling point. List the zone clearly when you advertise.

The city is organized around several business corridors. Downtown sits between Madison Avenue and the Saginaw River, the Banks district runs along Marquette Avenue, and the Broadway, Columbus and Johnson Street districts serve the surrounding blocks. Industrial pockets along Morton Street, Harrison Street, Woodside Avenue and the Marquette Industrial Center sit close to some of the older housing, which can affect noise and traffic for a buyer.

  • West Bay City on the west bank was its own city until the 1905 annexation.
  • The Center Avenue Historic District favors buyers who value large period houses and accept upkeep.
  • The Columbus Avenue business district runs out toward Bay Medical Center Hospital.

Match your marketing to the block. A cash buyer looks at condition first, while a retail buyer weighs school zone, commute and character.

Do Bay City rental rules affect a sale?

It does when the house has tenants or could be rented. The city requires every rental property to be registered, inspected and certified before a tenant occupies it, and the city's rental page carries the registration forms and a tenant complaint form. A rental that was never registered can come to light when a code officer visits, and that is better dealt with before a buyer's inspector finds it.

For a rental sale, pull together the registration, the certificate and any correction letters from past inspections. An investor taking over the tenants will ask for them, and an owner-occupant will want proof that every unit is legal.

Utilities add one local wrinkle. Bay City runs its own utility billing, and trash charges are placed on electric accounts for occupied and unoccupied homes alike. Settle the final bills and ask Utility Customer Service at 989-894-8104 about closing out the accounts at the transfer.

What will the Bay County Register of Deeds charge?

The Register of Deeds takes a flat $30 for each deed, mortgage or other instrument, however many pages it runs, and $4 of that is passed to the state survey and remonumentation fund. A warranty deed, land contract or condominium master deed also needs a tax certificate from the Bay County Treasurer, priced at $5 on its own check.

Two statutes produce the transfer tax. The county's posted schedule shows $7.50 for the state and $1.10 for the county on each thousand dollars of consideration. Together that is $8.60 per thousand, so a $100,000 sale owes $860.

Either the deed states the full price or an affidavit accompanies it, and a claimed exemption must be noted in the instrument itself. The state act exempts, for example, a gift deed to your child and a deed given in foreclosure.

How are Bay City property taxes handled when I sell?

The city side of collection comes first. From March 1, any unpaid residential tax is payable to the Bay County Treasurer at 515 Center Avenue (989-895-4285), where interest and fees build. Have the title company verify that summer and winter bills are settled or prorated before recording.

The state's default summer deadline is September 14, yet a charter can move it, so confirm Bay City's date with the Treasurer. Under the state schedule a late summer payment gains 1% a month, and whatever remains unpaid goes back to the county on March 1.

Anyone who claimed a principal residence exemption should send the rescind form to the city assessor within 90 days of leaving. The assessor can supply the form.

How do Bay City cash and listing proceeds compare?

Estimate your net on each path. On a listing, take away agent fees, repairs the buyer's inspection will request, transfer tax and the cost of carrying the house while you wait. On a cash offer, take away only what the buyer says you will pay, and have that stated in writing.

Ask each buyer who covers title and recording, whether the offer can shift after a walk-through, and which closing date is firm. A buyer worth dealing with answers plainly and lets you take time to compare.

Is a Bay City house with big repair needs still sellable?

Yes. An as-is buyer folds the repairs into the offer, and you can alternatively list at a lower price while disclosing known defects. Set the repair estimate beside the $97,600 middle home value in Bay City before you spend on renovation.

What transfer tax does a Bay City sale carry?

State tax of $7.50 and county tax of $1.10 per $1,000 combine to $8.60. On a $90,000 sale that is $774, which the seller pays unless the contract assigns it elsewhere.

Must a Bay City rental be registered before I sell?

The city requires registration, inspection and certification before any tenant moves in. If your house has been rented, collect the paperwork early, since buyers and title companies may request it.

Where do overdue Bay City taxes go after March 1?

They are payable to the Bay County Treasurer from that date. Clear the balance with the county or through the closing so the buyer receives clean title.

When does the Bay County deed get recorded?

The Register of Deeds records documents that meet its requirements and returns any that do not. Your title company normally submits the deed right after closing, so ask them for the recording confirmation date.

What happens when you sell a Jackson house?

Jackson is the seat of Jackson County. A sale there involves city hall on West Michigan Avenue, which handles assessing, treasury and rental registration, and the county, which handles recording. The house can be listed, sold privately, or bought as-is by a cash buyer, and the legal steps at closing match in every case. What differs is the house's condition and whether an owner or tenants live in it.

Jackson grew around the junction of I-94 and US 127, roughly 35 miles west of Ann Arbor, 35 miles south of Lansing, 75 miles west of Detroit and 65 miles east of Kalamazoo. It covers about 10.96 square miles. Mid-2025 estimates count 31,022 people, a 0.9 percent slip from the 2020 base.

What shaped the Jackson market and its older neighborhoods?

Horace Blackman claimed land here in 1829, and Jackson became a village in 1843 and a city in 1857. A county convention held under the oaks on July 6, 1854 carries a state historical marker identifying it as the birth of the Republican Party. Before Detroit built cars on assembly lines in 1910, Jackson factories were already making parts and assembling them, and more than 20 car brands once came from the city.

Heavy industry restructured around mid-century, which cost jobs and population. Three major private employers stand out: CMS Energy, which keeps its headquarters downtown, Henry Ford Health and Eaton. Michigan's first prison opened here in 1838, and a state corrections complex still operates in the area. Railroads made Jackson the crossroads of Michigan, and the Michigan Central depot on East Michigan Avenue is reported as the nation's oldest train station in continuous active use. Amtrak's Wolverine stops three times daily in each direction.

How affordable are Jackson homes?

Jackson sits at the low end of all four cities for both prices and rents. Survey figures for 2020 through 2024:

  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $103,200.
  • Homeownership: 54.7 percent of 13,281 households.
  • Typical rent: $898 a month.
  • Household size averages 2.29, and 16.1 percent of adults have finished a bachelor's degree.
  • Average trip to work: 17.0 minutes.

With a typical value near $103,000 and almost half of households renting, many Jackson houses belong to investors or need repairs, so buyers will scrutinize roofs, furnaces and foundations. If repair costs exceed what they would add to the price, an as-is sale to a cash buyer may be the simpler path.

What happens to rental registration when a Jackson rental sells?

Jackson keeps a registry of rentals that are not owner-occupied, and a sale restarts it. A registration is good for 3 years, owners report changes within 10 days, and renewals are due no later than 60 days before expiry. Selling voids the registration, and the new owner applies at closing. Within 45 days after the sale, the seller of a rented dwelling tells the Community Development Department who bought it and where to reach them.

A buyer who claims a 100 percent principal residence exemption with the city assessor skips registration. Anyone else registers within 45 days of closing, with a $5 per unit daily penalty for lateness. Fees are not refunded or credited on a transfer, so a seller who just paid for a registration cannot recover it.

What is Jackson's payment calendar for property taxes?

City bills arrive July 1 (summer) and December 1 (winter). Pay the summer bill in a lump by July 31, or split it into five payments due on the 20th from July to November. The winter bill is open for payment December 1 to February 14. Dates from the assessor's calendar:

Jackson assessing calendar for a property owner

Source: City of Jackson Assessor important dates and Treasurer pages.

Why will a buyer's Jackson tax bill likely exceed mine?

Michigan limits yearly growth of taxable value to the lesser of 5 percent or inflation, until a sale lifts the limit. After a transfer of ownership, MCL 211.27a resets taxable value for the following calendar year to the state equalized value, roughly half of market value. A long-time owner's bill probably sits well below what the next owner pays, so mention this early to serious buyers.

Sellers should also file a rescission of their principal residence exemption within 90 days of moving out (MCL 211.7cc), sending the form to the Jackson assessor.

Which Jackson employers and landmarks help a listing?

  • Dawn Foods, family-owned, has been based in Jackson since 1920.
  • Michigan Automotive Compressor is described as the largest manufacturer in the county and its fourth-largest single employer.
  • Reynolds Field, a general aviation airport of about 700 acres south of I-94, hosts the Jackson College Flight School and the annual Jackson Blues Festival in June.
  • Cell Block 7 Prison Museum occupies a closed cell block that was reopened to visitors.

Buyers who commute to Lansing, Ann Arbor or Detroit weigh the drive on I-94 and US 127, so state the exit and the time to each in your listing.

Will the city income tax follow me after I sell in Jackson?

Jackson levies its own income tax. Residents with income over $600 file and pay 1 percent; people who commute in to work pay 0.5 percent; corporations and partnerships pay 1 percent. Returns are due April 30, or the next business day when that date lands on a weekend. If you sell and move out of town, ask the treasurer's office how a part-year return works.

What will transfer tax cost on a Jackson sale?

Two Michigan taxes fall on the seller at recording: the state's $3.75 per $500 of price and the county's 55 cents per $500 where the county has fewer than 2,000,000 people. At the $103,200 median value, the price rounds up to 207 units of $500, or $890.10. Jackson County's Register of Deeds allows transfer tax to be folded into the recording fee on a single check payable to that office.

MCL 207.526 also exempts gifts to a child or grandchild, title-correction deeds and security instruments, and the county register posts its own exemption guidance.

What can I expect from Jackson's weather and schools when showing a house?

Winters here run cold and summers warm. The average January low is 17.5 degrees, the lowest reading on record is minus 20, and snowfall averages 37.3 inches a year, so a furnace and roof in good shape are real selling points. Almost the whole city lies inside Jackson Public Schools, with Jackson College, Baker College and Spring Arbor University among the local colleges. The city's parks department runs 26 parks totaling 645 acres, and JATA buses run ten routes Monday through Saturday from a downtown station. Mention these in listings for buyers who ask about commutes and schools.

What must a Jackson landlord tell the city after a sale?

Notify Community Development within 45 days, with the buyer's name and address. The buyer registers within 45 days after closing, unless they file a 100 percent principal residence exemption.

When are Jackson summer property taxes due?

In full by July 31, or in five installments on the 20th of July through November. Winter taxes can be paid December 1 through February 14.

Does Jackson tax income?

Yes. Residents with more than $600 in income pay 1 percent and nonresident workers pay 0.5 percent, with returns due April 30.

What transfer tax applies to a $103,200 Jackson sale?

$890.10, since the price rounds up to 207 units of $500, each carrying $3.75 state and $0.55 county tax (county under 2,000,000 residents). The seller pays at recording.

What is the deadline for a new Jackson owner's principal residence exemption?

June 1 for the summer bill. The owner must own and occupy the home by then, and the July Board of Review can fix missed claims.

Which ways of selling work for a Burton homeowner?

Choices in Burton run from a standard listing, to a private sale, to a cash deal with someone ready to absorb whatever work the house needs. All of them end with a deed recorded at the Genesee County Register of Deeds and transfer tax paid on the price.

Pick the route by looking at three things: how soon you must be out, what condition the house is in, and whether anything stands in the way of a clean title, such as back taxes, a lien or an unfinished estate. Patience and a house that shows well favor a listing. A seller who needs a firm date is better served by cash.

  • Agent listing: more buyers, but showings, appraisal and a buyer's lender add delay.
  • Private sale: no listing fee, with the paperwork on you.
  • Cash sale: fewer steps, and the buyer handles repairs after closing.

What should a seller notice about Burton itself?

Burton lies just outside Flint in Genesee County, and its roughly 29,300 residents make it the county's second largest city. It was Burton Township from 1856 and became a city in 1972 after residents voted to incorporate. Within city limits lie about 23 square miles of land.

Two named neighborhoods show how the area is laid out. Belsay lies on Belsay Road at the rail line north of I-69 and Court Street, and Lapeer Heights sits at Belsay and Roberta Roads south of Lapeer Road.

One recent change matters for utility costs: Burton began receiving Karegnondi Water Authority water, treated by the Genesee County Drain Commission, in December 2017. A buyer comparing monthly costs may ask about water bills, so keep a recent statement handy.

How does Burton's housing picture look in Census data?

Burton is a city of homeowners, with more than three in four households owning. The Census Bureau's figures are below.

Burton residents and housing, from Census QuickFacts

A population share of nearly one in five aged 65 or older means a good share of owners may be weighing a move to smaller housing or have inherited a house. If that is your situation, start by confirming who has legal authority to sign the deed.

How did Burton grow, and how does age show up in its houses?

Burton's population jumped from 2,154 in 1920 to 29,700 in 1960, and the census peak came in 1970 at 32,540. That growth points to a housing stock built largely in the mid-twentieth century. The count has drifted down since, to 29,715 in 2020 and an estimated 29,313 in 2025.

Early settlers arrived from Jefferson County, New York, and the first community was the Atherton settlement on Thread Creek in 1835. Over the years Flint annexed large pieces of the township's northern and western sides, which shaped the city's present boundaries.

For a seller, a house from the 1950s or 1960s can mean older plumbing, an aging furnace and a modest garage. The climate is humid continental, with warm summers and cold winters, so heating systems and roofs deserve attention before showings. Disclose what you know about them, and keep receipts for any work done.

Which Burton permit rules should you check before a sale?

Burton's Building Division publishes plain rules that decide whether past work will cause trouble with a buyer. The owner is responsible for making sure a permit was pulled, and unpermitted work can come up in an inspection or in the buyer's lender review.

  • A shed under 199 square feet needs a site permit; a structure of 200 square feet or more counts as a garage and needs a building permit.
  • Decks need permits unless they stand free at least 10 feet from the house and are under 200 square feet.
  • Finishing a basement requires a permit and an egress window.
  • In-ground pools need permits, and above-ground pools do when they stay up year round.
  • Cosmetic interior work such as paint and flooring needs no permit.

If you built a deck or finished the basement yourself, call the Building Division through City Hall and ask what is on file. Closing that gap before listing is cheaper than negotiating it afterward.

How do Burton property taxes work when a house sells?

Burton bills twice a year on deadlines of its own. Summer bills go out by July 1 and are due by September 30, and a one-time 4% penalty applies on October 1 with half a percent a month after that. Winter bills go out December 1 and are due by February 28. The city does not accept postmarks, so payment has to arrive at the Treasurer's office at 4303 S. Center Road by the due date.

On March 1 the account moves to the Genesee County Treasurer (810-257-3054), where a 4% collection fee and rising interest apply. The city states that property unpaid after two years is foreclosed and sold at auction.

The city's tax page also explains Proposal A: taxable value is capped at the lesser of inflation or 5% a year while the owner stays, but it can rise to the state equalized value after a transfer. A buyer's first bill can therefore exceed yours. New principal residence exemption applications reach the assessor by June 1, and a change of residence calls for an update form.

What are the Genesee County recording charges?

Recording at the Genesee County Register of Deeds costs a $30 flat fee for each document, whatever its length. Warranty deeds, land contracts and any deed containing a covenant of warranty need a $5 tax certification from the Genesee County Treasurer, paid on its own check.

The county's fee page lists $7.50 per thousand for the state and $1.10 per thousand for the county, which add up to $8.60. The seller is liable and the base is the price paid, so a $140,000 sale produces $1,204. Mortgages carry no transfer tax in Michigan.

A few transfers escape the tax, such as a gift deed to your child or a deed given in lieu of foreclosure, and the deed itself has to cite the exemption.

Is a cash buyer right for your Burton sale?

It can be, once the work a retail buyer would demand costs more than the discount a cash buyer applies. That happens with houses needing a roof or mechanical work, estates with several heirs, and landlord-owned houses with unpaid rent.

Gather your tax bill, any permit records and a recent water statement, and ask each buyer for a written offer that spells out who pays closing costs. Line up at least two before you sign anything.

Frequently asked questions

Does Burton demand an inspection before closing?

The Building Division grants building, site and occupancy permits. Ask it through City Hall whether your address needs any occupancy sign-off or has open permits before closing.

What does transfer tax cost on a Burton sale?

Genesee County posts a combined $8.60 for each $1,000 of price. At $120,000 that is $1,032, owed by the seller under the statute unless an exemption applies.

What are Burton's property tax deadlines?

Summer taxes are due by September 30 and winter taxes by February 28, according to the city Treasurer. After March 1, unpaid taxes go to the Genesee County Treasurer with added fees and interest.

Will unpermitted work block a Burton sale?

Not automatically, but expect questions. Permits are the owner's duty, and a buyer may ask for a discount or want the work legalized. A cash buyer usually accepts the condition and adjusts the price.

What becomes of my homestead exemption in a Burton sale?

It ends once the house is no longer your principal residence. Michigan expects a Request to Rescind (Form 2602) at the city assessor within 90 days, and each late day adds $5 until the $200 cap.

Oak Park is a Detroit-bordering suburb about 14 miles northwest of downtown, and it covers 5.16 square miles, all of it land. Eight Mile Road (M-102) forms the south edge and doubles as the Oakland and Wayne county line. Eleven Mile Road bounds the north, Greenfield Road the west, and I-696 clips the northern edge, with the Lodge Freeway (M-10) nearby.

The first major housing development went up in 1914. The village was incorporated in 1927 and the city on October 29, 1945. From 1950 to 1960 the population jumped from about 5,000 to above 36,000, and the city was called America's fastest growing. Parts of Royal Oak Township were annexed in 2002 and 2004. A FedEx distribution center on a 60-acre former armory site opened on March 31, 2017.

The Census Bureau estimates 29,072 residents for July 1, 2025, which is 1.7% below the 2020 base. At 5,743.2 people per square mile in 2020, Oak Park was more densely settled than Novi, Pontiac or Port Huron, so houses sit close together and street-level comparables carry weight.

For 2020 to 2024 the middle owner-occupied value was $212,300, rent in the middle of the range was $1,396 a month, and owners lived in 63.3% of homes. The city counts 12,452 households with a middle income of $71,510.

A boundary that follows a street means two neighbors can be in different districts. Check the exact address, especially in the strip near I-696 where Berkley applies.

Which Oak Park city charges can come up around a sale?

The city lists separate building, electrical and demolition permits, and the Building Division at 14300 Oak Park Boulevard takes building applications. It also publishes Roofing Guidelines for Residential Properties describing the roofing permit and the inspections a roof job requires.

If a prior owner did the roof, wiring or an addition, ask Municipal Services what is on record for your address. A missing final sign-off is cheaper to resolve before listing than after a buyer's inspector spots it. City code also asks owners, occupants and tenants to maintain the ground around their buildings, so cut back overgrowth and haul out debris before showings. Oak Park also requires a building permit before any demolition of a residential or commercial structure, so a seller who wants to remove a damaged garage or shed should apply first.

Clearing out a home is part of many sales. A residential garage sale needs a $10 permit from the City Clerk's Office, which asks for a state ID or driver's license showing the sale address.

Which forms go to the Oak Park assessor after a sale?

The Assessor's Office is at 14000 Oak Park Boulevard. Two filings follow a sale.

  • Property Transfer Affidavit: needed whenever ownership changes, including title, beneficial use or ownership interest, with a 45-day deadline from the transfer.
  • Request to Rescind Principal Residence Exemption: filed by homeowners who sell or convert their principal residence so the exemption ends.

The buyer files a new exemption form after closing; the city lists it as Form 2368 and takes it at the same Assessor's Office counter. Ask your closing agent which of these it handles so none is filed twice or skipped.

How is an Oak Park deed recorded at the county level?

The deed goes to the Oakland County Register of Deeds. Its fee page lists the county transfer tax as 55 cents for each $500 of consideration and the state tax as $3.75 for each $500. Consideration under $100.00 is exempt, and the reason for any exemption has to be written on the face of the document.

The office's question list adds a few requirements you can check in advance: notarized signatures, a 2-1/2 inch blank top margin, and an embossed seal on any death certificate filed. Its index reaches back to January 1, 1964, so you can pull your own earlier deed and confirm the legal description before signing.

Frequently asked questions

Is an inspection required before an Oak Park house is sold?

City pages list a certificate of occupancy for new or altered buildings and a rental inspection every two years or after a change in tenancy. Ask Municipal Services whether your house, particularly one that has been rented, needs either before a buyer moves in.

What does a certificate of occupancy cost in Oak Park?

The fee schedule prints $50 for occupancy only and $50 for reissuance. Commercial and renovation certificates carry different amounts on the same schedule.

Should an Oak Park seller do anything about the alarm permit?

The city's alarm page states a one-time $20 fee and says each change in ownership of an operable alarm system requires a new permit. Tell the buyer so they register the system in their own name.

What is the deadline for the Property Transfer Affidavit in Oak Park?

Forty-five days from the transfer, filed at the Assessor's Office, 14000 Oak Park Boulevard. It covers any change in title, beneficial use or ownership interest.

Where does the deed for an Oak Park house get filed?

At the Oakland County Register of Deeds. A warranty deed is first tax certified at the county treasurer's office for $5.00, and recording costs $30.00.

The city is a Downriver suburb in Wayne County, near 14 miles southwest of downtown Detroit. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 28,931 residents, below the 30,014 counted in 2020. You can reach a buyer in three common ways:

  • A private sale leaves pricing, the contract and the inspection with you.

Whichever you pick, read who pays the inspection fee, who does repairs and when funds arrive.

How does the Southgate resale inspection work?

The city checks the outside of each dwelling before it changes hands. According to its Home Sales page, a certificate covers a single sale or transfer, and the next owner who sells needs a fresh inspection.

  • Fee: $200 for the first visit as of June 1, 2024, then $60 for every extra visit.
  • Path one: correct each cited item and collect the certificate.
  • Path two: sell as-is. The buyer signs an affidavit assuming the violations plus an escrow agreement, and deposits $1,000 before closing. That affidavit then doubles as the closing document.
  • Reports come by email, mail or pickup within 5 business days of the visit.

Have the certificate or the buyer's signed affidavit ready before you book a closing. Home Sales is its own department at City Hall, separate from the Building Department, with its own line at (734) 258-7783.

Home Sales answers on weekdays and closes for lunch between noon and 1:00 p.m. Its page links an application, an inspection checklist and an online invoice payment, so read the checklist before the inspector comes.

The city certificate and the county recording step both sit between an accepted offer and a closing, so sequence them.

  2. Choose between correcting the cited items and letting the buyer assume them.
  3. Hold the certificate or the signed affidavit before a closing date is set.
  4. Have your title company line up tax certification for a warranty deed.
  5. Record the deed with the county and pay transfer tax then unless an exemption applies.

What is Southgate like for a home seller?

Southgate covers 6.875 square miles with no water. The city was cut from Ecorse Township and incorporated on October 8, 1958.

Wayne County moved to a new fee schedule on January 1, 2026: a $26 base and a $4 state survey fee, $30 per deed. Transfer tax comes due at recording unless a proper exemption is noted, and the office prints $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state.

  • A warranty deed, a deed with a warranty covenant or a land contract needs Wayne County Treasurer certification before recording.
  • Cards need matching ID, and American Express and Discover are refused.
  • Mailed personal checks are accepted, counter ones are not, and each document needs its own check.

No. It covers one sale or transfer, and each later sale needs a new inspection.

Wayne County lists $30 per document under its January 1, 2026 schedule, with transfer tax paid at recording. Your title company can total the figures.

Households average 2.08 people, and in the 2020 count 38.8% of them were a single person living alone. The 2020 count found 13,993 housing units, 5.0% of them vacant, and a homeowner vacancy rate of 1.0%.

What is the city of Madison Heights like?

Madison Heights is a compact Oakland County city about 12 miles north of downtown Detroit. Voters made it a city on January 17, 1955, after it had belonged to Royal Oak Township.

Troy, Royal Oak, Hazel Park and Warren ring the city, and its eastern edge at Dequindre Road doubles as the line between Oakland and Macomb counties. I-75 skirts the west side while I-696 marks much of the south. Of the 112 miles of roadway, the city maintains 105. About 91% of its buildings are single-family homes or condominiums, roughly 9,800 owners, yet light industrial and commercial property supplies around 60% of the tax base.

  • Schools: Madison District Public Schools and Lamphere Public Schools serve different addresses. Bishop Foley Catholic High School is private, and Four Corners Montessori Academy operates as a charter.
  • Employers: the city belongs to Oakland County's Automation Alley and has more than 1,300 commercial and industrial businesses.
  • Community: 168 Asian Mart, at 38,000 square feet, is described as the largest Asian supermarket in southeast Michigan, and a Chinese cultural center sits in the city.
  • Education: 90.4% of adults finished high school and 33.9% have at least a bachelor's degree.

The commercial side is large for a city of seven square miles: 23 shopping centers, 11 hotels and seven industrial parks. The city also hosts the George W. Kuhn Retention and Treatment Basin, a stormwater facility that serves southeast Oakland County. Residents are a mixed group, with 15.0% using another language at home, 12.8% foreign-born and 909 veterans, and 87.5% had not moved in the past year.

Will Madison Heights make me pass an inspection to sell?

No. City staff state that Madison Heights neither requires nor provides resale inspections, so you can list or sign a purchase agreement without booking a walk-through.

Rentals are a separate matter. An owner who lets someone else live in a Madison Heights house needs a landlord license, even when no rent is charged. A qualified relative living there waives both the fee and the inspection. Without a license, an owner cannot collect rent or evict, a point worth settling before a tenant-occupied house goes on the market.

Madison Heights landlord license fees
Property typeFee, new or renewal
Single-family home$210
Up to four units$245
Five or more units$47.50 per unit

Source: City of Madison Heights landlord licensing page. The first license may run under three years with a prorated fee, and each renewal covers four years and brings a fresh inspection. The city will not issue a license while property taxes, special assessments or water bills are unpaid.

How do Madison Heights tax bills and deadlines work?

The city's treasury handles both bills directly. Early July brings the summer bill, payable through August 31 with no penalty, and early December brings the winter bill, payable through February 17.

After August 31, a 4% penalty applies from September 1, and a further 1/2% accrues each month. Winter bills pick up a 3% penalty on February 18. City Hall stops taking payment after March 2, and from March 3 the Oakland County Treasurer collects, with extra penalties added. A drop box outside City Hall takes checks and money orders around the clock.

A sale reopens the next owner's number. In the year after a transfer, taxable value jumps to the state equalized value under MCL 211.27a, so a long-held house that has been capped for decades can produce a much larger bill for the buyer. If you took the principal residence exemption, file a rescission after you move out; MCL 211.7cc sets a 90-day window and charges $5 a day, to a maximum of $200, for lateness. Closing agents must give both sides the affidavit and rescission forms at the table.

Which documents and fees come with a Madison Heights closing?

A typical closing here involves a recorded deed, a tax certification if the deed carries a warranty, transfer tax and the city affidavit. A title company usually takes care of the deed work and the certificate.

  • Recording: Oakland County's Register of Deeds examines each document before recording it. The page needs a 2.5 inch margin at the top and a notary's signature.
  • Tax certification: taxes must show as current on a warranty deed, and the county charges $5.
  • Transfer tax: state and county tax together run $4.30 per $500 of price, so a $200,000 sale costs $1,720. Gifts to a child or grandchild are exempt under MCL 207.526.
  • City affidavit: file it with the Assessing Department at 300 W Thirteen Mile Road within 45 days. A late residential filing costs $5 a day up to $200, and commercial or industrial property costs $25 a day up to $1,000.

Ask the Oakland County Register of Deeds for the current recording fee before mailing anything. Its Sheriff Deed and Clerk Deed redemption desk is a separate service and does not affect an ordinary sale.

Which sale route fits a Madison Heights house?

Pick by how much time you have and what shape the house is in. Compare each route by the money left after repairs, carrying costs and closing fees, since a high list price can shrink quickly.

  • Agent listing: showings and wide exposure, with the buyer's lender and appraisal setting the timeline.
  • For sale by owner: full control of price and terms, and the disclosures and paperwork fall on you.
  • Cash purchase: no lender step, and the buyer takes the house with its repairs or a tenant already inside.

If a cash sale appeals, tell us the Madison Heights address and what shape the place is in, and we will price it as it stands.

Frequently asked questions

Does Madison Heights inspect houses at resale?

No. The city does not require or provide resale inspections. Inspections come up only with landlord licensing, and an owner-occupied sale does not trigger one.

Can a tenant stay in the house while I sell it?

Yes, provided the house carries a city landlord license. The landlord license is mandatory for any occupied home the owner does not live in, though a qualified relative waives the fee and inspection. Without it, rent collection and eviction are off the table.

What would transfer tax cost on a $200,000 Madison Heights house?

$1,720, made up of $1,500 in state tax and $220 in county tax. The deed has to show the value or carry an affidavit stating it.

Where do I send Madison Heights taxes after March 2?

To the Oakland County Treasurer. City Hall accepts payment only through March 2, and the county adds penalties after that.

What happens if I file the transfer affidavit late?

The city fines $5 per day up to $200 for a residential property. The deadline is 45 days after the transfer, and the form goes to the Assessing Department.

What are the realistic ways to sell in Port Huron?

Port Huron homeowners can put the house on the market with an agent, handle a private sale, or deal with a buyer who purchases houses outright. The city is the St. Clair County seat, so the county's land records office sits inside city limits.

How quickly a sale closes comes down to what is left unresolved. Clear title, permits on file and an empty house move fast on any route. An unpaid tax bill, a missing permit or a lease in place slows things, and the buyer either waits for a fix or discounts the price. The sections below cover what the city and county ask for, so you can clear those items early.

Where does Port Huron sit and what shapes its housing?

Port Huron stands where Lake Huron narrows into the St. Clair River, facing Sarnia, Ontario across the water. The Blue Water Bridge links the two cities at the eastern end of I-69 and I-94. The city's total area is 12.26 square miles, though only 8.08 of that is land, and the Black River splits the city in half before reaching the St. Clair near downtown.

The U.S. built Fort Gratiot here in 1814, the city incorporated in 1857, and it became the county seat in 1871. A fire swept through on October 8, 1871, and an F4 tornado on May 21, 1953 damaged or destroyed over 400 structures. The village of Fort Gratiot was annexed in 1895. Shipbuilding and lumber work pulled in immigrants in the 1850s, and auto-parts makers followed later.

The 2020 census counted 28,983 residents. The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 28,273, a 2.4% decline. Over 8.10 square miles of land, density was 3,577.3 people per square mile.

How do Port Huron home values and incomes look?

The middle owner-occupied home in Port Huron was valued at $149,300 for 2020 to 2024, with a middle rent of $982. Owners live in 61.7% of the homes.

  • Households: 12,734, averaging 2.21 people.
  • Middle household income: $50,366.
  • Middle monthly owner costs: $1,140 with a mortgage and $562 without.
  • Residents 65 or older: 18.0%, a larger share than in Novi, Oak Park or Pontiac.
  • Average commute: 20.8 minutes.

A house inherited from an older relative needs its title and probate steps finished before it can be listed, so start those early. Port Huron's median owner-occupied value is well under Novi's but above Pontiac's, so recent sales nearby are the best guide to a fair price.

How do lake-effect winters and the waterfront affect a Port Huron house?

NOAA's 1991 to 2020 normals give Port Huron 34.87 inches of precipitation and 35.5 inches of snow in a year, spread over 22 snowy days. January averages a low of 19.9 F, the record low is minus 19 F, and the July average high is 81.3 F.

With so much shoreline, flood mapping matters. The city's planning page links flood maps, and the building page says a property in a flood plain or zone may need EGLE Water Resources approval for exterior projects. Ask the Building Inspection Division whether your parcel is mapped before you list.

What draws buyers to Port Huron?

Water access is the main draw. The city owns 17 waterfront areas covering 102 acres with 3.5 miles of frontage, three public beaches and the largest municipal marina system in Michigan, with five mooring locations. It also has 14 public parks and a community center.

Work comes from auto-parts makers such as SMR Automotive and International Automotive Components, plus two acute care hospitals, McLaren Port Huron and Lake Huron Medical Center. St. Clair County Community College is in the city, and Port Huron High School and Port Huron Northern High School serve students.

Which Port Huron permits come up before a sale?

The city's Building Inspection page spells out what needs a permit, and a buyer's inspector often checks the same things. The table sorts the common ones.

Permit categories on the Port Huron building page
Permit typeExamples listed
Building permitRoofs, windows, doors, siding, decks, porches, garages, basement finishes, interior and exterior alterations
Zoning permitFences, driveways, concrete patios, hot tubs, playground equipment, pools over 24 inches deep

No permit neededPainting, carpeting, tile, replacing kitchen cabinets in the same layout

The page lists the risks of skipping a permit: safety problems, fines, possibly tearing the structure down, and trouble if you later decide to sell. An owner may pull permits in place of a contractor only as the registered legal owner living in the house as a primary residence. Properties in the Historic District need Historic District Commission approval for exterior work. The Building Inspection Division answers at (810) 984-9733.

Does Port Huron oversee rental or vacant houses?

It does. The planning department runs a Rental Certification Program, and its document center posts a Foreclosed, Vacant and Abandoned Property Registration Form. If your house has been rented or sits empty, ask the Building Inspection Division what registration or certification applies to the address and whether it passes to a buyer.

Houses inside the historic area fall under Chapter 52-576 through 52-591 of the city's Historic District ordinance, which requires a work permit for alterations, significant repairs, new construction, demolition and moving.

What happens at the St. Clair County land records office?

The register's office is at 200 Grand River Avenue, Suite 103, Port Huron, phone (810) 989-6930. Monday through Thursday it works from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Friday from 10:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with a lunch closing from noon to 1:00 p.m. The recording counter shuts at 4:00 p.m., and anything received later is dated 8:00 a.m. on the next business day.

  • Recording charge: a flat $30.00 for each document whatever its page count, plus $3.00 after the first instrument reference.
  • Certified copy of a recorded document: $5.00.
  • Tax certificate: required before recording a warranty deed, a land contract, or any deed with a warranty covenant, under MCL 211.135. The treasurer certifies over the counter from 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., closed noon to 1:00 p.m.
  • Transfer tax as the county's page prints it: $1.10 for each thousand dollars of sale amount for the county and $7.50 for each thousand for the state.

Land records can be viewed online from 1984 forward, and the office runs a Property Fraud Alert sign-up. Most sellers let the closing agent carry the deed in.

Frequently asked questions

How soon can a Port Huron sale close?

It depends on title, taxes and any tenant. At the recording end, the St. Clair County counter closes at 4:00 p.m., and a document received after that is dated 8:00 a.m. the next business day.

Do I need a permit for work I did before selling in Port Huron?

Roofs, windows, doors, siding, decks, garages and basement finishes need a building permit, and furnaces, water heaters and sump pumps need trade permits. The city's page says skipping one can cause problems when you sell.

Where is a Port Huron deed recorded?

At the St. Clair County Register of Deeds, 200 Grand River Avenue, Suite 103. A warranty deed needs a county treasurer's tax certificate first.

What transfer tax does St. Clair County print?

The Register of Deeds fee page prints $1.10 per thousand dollars of sale amount for the county and $7.50 per thousand for the state. Your closing statement shows the exact dollar amounts for your sale.

Are there flood zones to check before listing in Port Huron?

Yes. The city links flood maps on its planning page, and a property in a flood plain may need state approval for exterior projects. Call the Building Inspection Division at (810) 984-9733 to learn whether your parcel is mapped.

Why does the city inspection decide how an Allen Park sale goes?

Because no Allen Park house closes without a Certificate of Occupancy or a signed buyer affidavit, and each takes some days to arrange. The rule covers homes first listed on or after March 1, 2022, under Chapter 10, Article 10, Section 10-404 of the city code.

Build your schedule backward from it. Request the inspection first, read what the inspector cites, and then choose between repairing the items and handing them to a buyer who accepts them.

How does the Allen Park sales inspection work?

The Building Department walks the interior and the outside of the lot, and the fee of $175 pays for both the first visit and the follow-up. The city publishes a list of the most common violations and an application form, so you can check your own house before the inspector arrives.

  • Fix every cited item and the department issues the Certificate of Occupancy.
  • Or sell as is, which requires the buyer to sign an affidavit accepting the violations.
  • The buyer also puts at least $500 into escrow, and 10 percent of it cannot be refunded.
  • That affidavit takes the place of the certificate as the closing document.
  • Reports can be mailed or picked up within 5 business days of the inspection.

Phone the Building Department at 313-928-4441 or 313-928-4134 to schedule. The city's advice to sellers is plain: do not set a closing date until you hold the certificate or the buyer's signed affidavit.

What is Allen Park like as a place to sell?

Allen Park is a small Downriver city, 7.00 square miles of land, about 12 miles from downtown Detroit. Ford offices and facilities sit inside it, the Detroit Lions train and keep their headquarters here, and the Uniroyal Giant Tire, a former World's Fair Ferris wheel moved to the city in 1966, is its best-known landmark.

A village from 1927 and a city since 1957, Allen Park took its name from a lawyer and lumberman who held land across what is now Allen Park and Melvindale. Its population leaped from 12,329 in 1950 to 37,494 in 1960 and topped out at 40,747 in 1970, which is why so many of its brick houses date from the postwar boom. The 2020 count was 28,638, and the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate is 27,445.

Neighbors on the map are Dearborn, Dearborn Heights, Melvindale, Lincoln Park, Southgate and Taylor. I-94 crosses the north end, I-75 clips the southeast corner, and Southfield Road (M-39) slices through as an eight-lane boulevard. The Fairlane Green shopping center opened in 2006, and the city once earned a spot on a magazine's list of top small cities.

Bowlers know the city too: Thunderbowl Lanes hosted the 2009 PBA World Series of Bowling. In 1950 the area directly west of Melvindale still belonged to Ecorse Township, a reminder that the city's current shape came together in stages after incorporation.

Which school district does an Allen Park address belong to?

It depends on the street. Most of the city sits in the Allen Park School District, which runs Arno, Lindemann and Bennie elementary schools plus Allen Park Middle School and Allen Park High School. The north end is part of Melvindale-Northern Allen Park Public Schools, and the area south of the Sexton-Kilfoil Drain falls in the Southgate Community School District.

Allen Park High School opened in 1950, and before that local students finished the eighth grade at Lapham school and then traveled to other cities for high school. Inter-City Baptist School and the St. Frances Cabrini schools, including Cabrini High School, are the local private options. Put the district name in your listing, since families shopping by school will filter by it.

What do the numbers say about Allen Park homes and households?

Daily life figures round out the picture. Workers average a 23.8 minute trip to work, 66.1 percent of residents over 16 are in the labor force, and 31.0 percent of adults over 25 hold a bachelor's degree. The poverty rate is 6.9 percent, 91.1 percent of households have broadband, and the city counts 1,301 veterans, which is useful context for a seller wondering who the local buyers are.

What does Wayne County charge to record an Allen Park deed?

Recording costs $30 per document, split as $26 for the register plus a $4 state survey and remonumentation fee. That schedule started January 1, 2026, the first increase at the office since 1996.

Transfer tax comes due at recording, at $3.75 per $500 for the state and $0.55 per $500 for the county. A $185,000 house produces a combined $1,591, and the seller bears it. Warranty deeds must carry a certification from the Wayne County Treasurer before they are recorded.

Payment rules differ from other counties:

  • Debit and credit cards work over the counter with matching ID, and are refused for mailed items.
  • A personal check can be mailed, but the counter will not take one.
  • The office does not process American Express or Discover.
  • One check per document, for the exact total: an overpayment above $25 returns the papers.

The office answers questions at (313) 224-5851.

Why does the Wayne County Register of Deeds reject deeds?

The office publishes its own list of repeat offenders. Photocopied signatures fail. So does a deed with no stated price and no exemption cited, a thin legal description, a notary block that is hard to read, or no return address for the recorded copy. Parcel number and street address belong on the page as well.

One flawed document sinks a whole bundle paid with a single check. Have the drafter run the checklist ahead of closing and confirm the treasurer has certified the deed.

What changes if the Allen Park house is a rental?

Every rental house must hold a Certificate of Compliance before anyone occupies it. Registration costs $200 at first, renewal costs $175, and each certificate lasts three years.

City rental inspectors work Tuesdays and Thursdays only, using the same Building Department phone numbers as the sales inspection. Landlords whose house is not rented can file a non-rental affidavit. If a tenant lives in the house when you sell, expect scheduling work for the interior inspection, and a buyer who will keep renting should ask for the date of your current certificate.

Frequently asked questions

Which Allen Park homes are exempt from the occupancy certificate?

Homes that were listed before March 1, 2022. Anything listed on or after that date needs the certificate or a buyer's signed affidavit before closing.

What do I get for the $175 city inspection fee?

One initial walk-through and one final visit. Reports are mailed or held for pickup within 5 business days.

How do I estimate transfer tax on an Allen Park house?

Take the price in thousands and multiply by $8.60. That blends the state share of $3.75 per $500 with the county share of $0.55 per $500, so $185,000 yields $1,591 owed by the seller.

Where does an Allen Park deed get recorded?

At the Wayne County Register of Deeds, which has charged $30 per document since January 1, 2026. Warranty deeds go to the county treasurer for certification first.

Can I close with open violations on the Allen Park house?

Yes, if the buyer signs the city affidavit and escrows at least $500. The buyer then handles the repairs after closing.

What does a Hamtramck seller deal with first?

Hamtramck is a two-square-mile city in Wayne County that sits almost entirely inside Detroit's borders, so a sale here follows Hamtramck's own city code and Wayne County's tax process, which differ from Detroit's. Whether the house goes to market, to a neighbor, or to a cash buyer, it passes three local checkpoints: the city's pre-sale inspection rules, the treasurer's tax calendar, and the assessor's transfer paperwork.

The city covers 2.09 square miles, all of it land, and Interstate 75 runs roughly along its western edge with I-94 near the southern edge. Downtown Detroit is about 5 miles south. Census estimates for mid-2025 count 27,261 people, 4.1 percent fewer than the 2020 base. Expect sales to be decided block by block rather than by a citywide trend.

How did Hamtramck's housing stock come about?

Most of the older homes trace back to the factory boom. The Dodge Brothers plant opened in 1914, and Hamtramck's population jumped by more than 1,200 percent between 1910 and 1920 as workers moved close to the line. The village became a city in 1922, partly to resist annexation by Detroit. Around 1925, about 78 percent of households owned their homes or were paying one off.

That history explains what a buyer finds inside a typical house: compact lots, frame houses and flats built close together, and many decades of owners making their own repairs. Polish families gave way over time to immigrants from Yemen, Bangladesh, Pakistan and the Balkans, and a 2018 survey found schoolchildren speaking 16 native languages. Houses that changed hands inside one family for generations often carry unrecorded repairs, old liens or unclear titles, so clear those up before you pick an asking price.

How big are Hamtramck households, and what do homes cost?

Survey estimates covering 2020 through 2024 paint an unusual picture. Treat them as a starting point for pricing, not a final answer.

  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $131,000.
  • Homeownership: 58.3 percent among 7,120 households.
  • Persons per household: 3.86, which points to large households and heavily used kitchens and baths.
  • Typical rent: $989 a month.
  • Foreign-born residents make up 46.7 percent of the city, and 73.5 percent of people age 5 and over speak another language at home.

Because of those household sizes, a house with extra bedrooms or a finished basement often draws more interest than the same square footage elsewhere. Say plainly in your listing or conversation which rooms are legal bedrooms.

Must I pass a city inspection to sell in Hamtramck?

Only for some owners. Under the city's pre-sale subchapter (sections 150.201 to 150.206), a property holding a Neighborhood Enterprise Zone certificate cannot change hands, through a broker or otherwise, unless the Building Department has issued a current certificate of approval. Everyone else may request a voluntary inspection, but once you file that request you cannot withdraw it, and every violation found must be fixed to earn the certificate.

The same code gives you a way through if repairs would delay closing. The city refuses a transfer affidavit for an NEZ home that lacks the certificate, with one exception: the buyer may sign a notarized statement promising to fix every listed violation within six months. A few more details matter:

  • Both the inspection report and the certificate of approval last twelve months.
  • If the building official sees serious neglect or hazards, a mandatory inspection can be ordered whatever the NEZ status.
  • A certificate guarantees nothing about condition; the city accepts no liability for concealed defects, mold or asbestos.

Before signing a purchase agreement, call the Building Department and ask whether your parcel has an NEZ certificate.

What if the house is vacant, foreclosed or a rental?

Chapter 96 of the city code covers houses that have sat empty. A home vacant for 180 days or more, or one that any lender, county or other holder has foreclosed, cannot be occupied until the Department of Public Services issues a certificate of occupancy. Getting it takes an inspection, correction of every violation, and payment of back property tax, special assessments, water and sewer bills and city cleanup charges.

Rentals fall under Chapter 150. Landlords hold a certificate of compliance good for two years at first and three years at each renewal. A sale ends that certificate at once, and the buyer has 30 days after the ownership change to apply for a new one. A landlord with a notice of violation outstanding must hand the buyer a copy and file the buyer's notarized acknowledgment with the building official before conveying the property, land contracts included.

What are the Hamtramck tax deadlines, and what happens after them?

Bills come out on July 1 and December 1 and are paid at the city treasurer's office. Whatever remains after the city's February 28 cutoff passes to the Wayne County Treasurer, where the cost climbs. The table follows a parcel that stays unpaid.

Hamtramck and Wayne County tax calendar for an unpaid parcel
StageWhat happens
July 1Summer bill issued; full payment due August 20, or half in July with the rest by December 30
December 1Winter bill issued; due by February 15
February 28Final day to pay the city treasurer
March 1County takes over collection: a 4 percent fee plus 1 percent interest every month
March 1, a year after thatParcel forfeits; a $175 fee applies and monthly interest climbs to 1.5 percent
March 31 and April 1, a year after forfeitureCourt judgment; ownership moves to the county unless the owner redeems

Source: Hamtramck Treasurer and Wayne County Treasurer timeline pages. Foreclosed homes are then offered at public auction in September and October, so a seller with two years of arrears has a hard deadline.

What paperwork does the assessor need after a Hamtramck sale?

Buyers have 45 days after closing to file a Property Transfer Affidavit with the assessor; late filers can be charged $5 a day, capped at $200. Sellers sign a rescission request for their principal residence exemption so the claim leaves the parcel, since a missed rescission can turn into a bill if the state audits. A buyer who moves in files a fresh exemption affidavit, worth 18 mills of school operating tax.

State law also uncaps taxable value on a sale (MCL 211.27a): for the next calendar year it equals the state equalized value, roughly half of market price, which can push the buyer's first bill above yours. Assessment appeals go to the March Board of Review.

What transfer tax applies to a Hamtramck deed?

Michigan puts the transfer tax on the seller: $3.75 per $500 of price at the state level (MCL 207.525) plus a county levy under MCL 207.504 of 55 cents per $500 below 2,000,000 residents, capped at 75 cents above that. The county treasurer collects both within 15 days after the deed is handed over.

MCL 207.526 exempts family conveyances to a child or grandchild, judgments that name no price, and deeds issued in foreclosing government-backed loans. Confirm the county rate and the recording fee with Wayne County before closing.

Does Hamtramck have a local income tax I should plan for?

Yes. Hamtramck is one of the Michigan cities with its own income tax, at 1.00 percent for residents and 0.50 percent for nonresidents. Ask the city income tax office how a move out of town or rental income affects your filing.

Frequently asked questions

Is a certificate of approval mandatory for my Hamtramck sale?

Only when the property holds a Neighborhood Enterprise Zone certificate. Other owners may ask for a voluntary inspection, though a filed request cannot be pulled back. In an NEZ sale, a buyer can offer a notarized repair promise in place of the certificate.

When is the Hamtramck summer tax bill due?

August 20 for the full amount. Paying half in July moves the rest to December 30. Winter bills are due February 15, and unpaid balances pass to Wayne County on March 1.

What is the foreclosure timeline for unpaid Hamtramck taxes?

About two years. Roughly two years from the first delinquency. Wayne County takes over on March 1, forfeits the parcel a year later, and a circuit court judgment follows. Owners can redeem through March 31 of the foreclosure year by paying taxes, interest and fees.

Which forms follow a Hamtramck closing?

The buyer files a transfer affidavit within 45 days, and the seller files a rescission of the principal residence exemption. A buyer who will live there also files a new exemption affidavit.

Does a Hamtramck rental certificate carry over to a buyer?

It does not. The certificate ends at the sale, and the new owner applies for another within 30 days of the ownership change.

Why does the inspection step set the pace of a Garden City sale?

A house cannot change occupants in Garden City until the city issues a certificate of occupancy, so the inspection calendar often matters more than the buyer's financing. The city is a compact Wayne County suburb of 5.87 square miles, roughly 15 miles west of downtown Detroit. A seller who books that inspection early can build the closing around it.

The notes below cover the inspection, the permit rules behind repairs, the city's housing figures, schools and services, and what follows a transfer of title.

How did Garden City get its layout and its name?

The name echoes the English garden city movement of the nineteenth century, and most early home sites were laid out as one-acre plots so a family could raise its own fruit and vegetables. Garden City became a village within Nankin Township in June 1927 and a city six years later. Most lots are now far smaller, some only 40 by 135 feet.

Counts climbed from 9,012 in 1950 to 38,017 in 1960 and topped out at 41,864 in 1970, before easing to 27,380 in 2020. Local landmarks include the site of the first Kmart, which opened in 1962 and has since been demolished, and Henry Ford's honeymoon cottage, moved here from Dearborn in 1952. Downtown centers on the corner of Ford and Middlebelt Roads.

  • The city's population quadrupled between 1950 and 1960, so much of the housing is now more than 60 years old.
  • Lots as small as 40 by 135 feet leave little room for additions or large outbuildings.
  • Ford Road and Middlebelt Road are the main corridors for commuting and errands.

This is a city of homeowners: QuickFacts shows nearly four of every five homes occupied by their owners.

How does the Garden City certificate of occupancy work for a seller?

Whenever a property is sold, the city wants a certificate of occupancy in place before the buyer moves in. The Building Department schedules the inspection, which takes place Monday through Thursday, with a morning window from 9 a.m. to noon and an afternoon window from noon to 4 p.m. The department's FAQ lists a $200 fee, payable when the inspection date is booked, and says the certificate is good for one year.

The city warns that spring and summer are the busy season, and that a seller may wait three to six weeks for an inspection. Someone who needs a fast closing should reserve the slot the day a contract is signed, or sooner. The Building Department number is (734) 793-1650.

  • Reserve an inspection date when the home is listed or under contract.
  • Fix visible safety items first, since a failed inspection means a reinspection and more waiting.
  • The city's FAQ suggests a December or January certificate is ready for an immediate closing.

Which repairs need a permit in Garden City?

A permit is good for six months, and all inspections must happen inside that window. Roof, windows, exterior doors, siding, gutters and kitchen or bathroom remodels need a building permit. Water tanks, furnaces, air conditioners and generators need mechanical permits. Service panels, circuits, fixtures and hard-wired smoke detectors need electrical permits, and sewer repairs, sinks, toilets and showers need plumbing permits. Driveways, easement walks, patios and porch caps fall under a flatwork permit.

Sheds under 200 square feet need no building permit but still need a flatwork permit for the slab. An owner living in the house may pull personal permits, and anyone who hires a contractor should require the contractor to pull them, at the same cost. Ask the Building Department whether any open permit on the address could affect the certificate before you list.

What happens if the house is a rental?

Garden City runs a rental certification program through its Ordinance Department at the police department, reachable at (734) 793-1748. Rental certifications run three years, and the owner must recertify before the term ends. A landlord selling the house should confirm that the certification is current and say whether tenants will stay.

An investor buying it should ask the Ordinance Department how the transfer affects that certification.

What do schools and city services add to a Garden City listing?

The Garden City School District runs four elementary schools, a middle school, Garden City High School, home of the Cougars, and Cambridge High School as its alternative program. Tipton Academy, a charter school, serves pre-kindergarten through seventh grade. St. Raphael Catholic School closed in 2016, and the former Radcliff Middle School building became a recreation center the city bought from Schoolcraft College.

Residents receive a free 95-gallon trash container from the city's refuse contractor, and curbside recycling carts can be delivered on request. Yard waste pickup runs from the first full week of April until about the middle of December, with Christmas trees collected after December 25. Buyers ask about such basics, so mention them when you describe the property.

What does the Michigan transfer tax cost on a Garden City sale?

Michigan's two transfer taxes, both paid by the seller, are 55 cents for the county and $3.75 for the state on every $500 of price (MCL 207.504 and 207.525). The county treasurer collects within 15 days after the deed is delivered (MCL 207.523).

A sale at Garden City's median value of $168,800 owes roughly $1,460, and the settlement statement shows the exact figure. The buyer then notifies the assessor within 45 days so taxable value can reset to the state equalized value the next year (MCL 211.27a). Ask the assessor for an estimate of the new owner's bill.

When does an as-is sale make sense for a Garden City house?

A small, well-kept house on a standard lot can sell through a listing, though the inspection queue and the buyer's loan both add time. A house that needs work to pass the certificate of occupancy, an estate property, or a seller facing a short deadline often does better with an as-is purchase.

  • A listing fits a house in good repair when you can wait out the inspection queue.
  • An as-is buyer fits a house where the inspector will likely list repairs you would rather not manage.
  • Get written agreement on who pays the inspection fee and handles any reinspection.

Weigh offers by what you keep after transfer tax, prorated taxes and credits, and write the closing date into the contract.

Must a Garden City house pass inspection before it changes hands?

Yes. The city requires a certificate of occupancy whenever a property is sold, and the new owner cannot occupy the house without it. The Building Department at (734) 793-1650 books the inspection.

How long is the wait for the Garden City inspection?

The city says a seller may wait three to six weeks in spring and summer. Booking early, or aiming for winter, shortens the wait.

What does the Garden City certificate of occupancy cost?

The city's FAQ lists $200, paid when the inspection is scheduled, for a certificate good for one year. Confirm the amount with the Building Department.

Will a Garden City buyer's tax bill run higher than mine?

Often. Taxable value resets to the state equalized value in the calendar year after the transfer, and the buyer must notify the assessor within 45 days.

Can I still sell a house that fails the inspection?

Yes, but the certificate has to be issued before the new owner moves in. Some sellers make the repairs, and others sell as-is and let the buyer finish them and request the reinspection.

How do Auburn Hills' rental and vacancy rules touch a home sale?

They matter whenever a buyer plans to rent the house or when the house sits empty before closing. The city's Community Development Department registers every detached one-family home that is rented or offered for rent, and it keeps a separate registry for vacant homes.

  • Rental registration costs $200, the permit to occupy $50, and the yearly renewal $250, due December 31.
  • Instead of filing a self-certification checklist, an owner can pay $155 for a city interior inspection.
  • A $100 penalty applies to a first failure to register, and civil infraction tickets can follow.
  • A buyer of an existing rental has 30 days from the sale to register again and obtain a new permit.
  • A vacant home must be registered within 30 days, and the vacant-home form lists a $355 fee.

A letter from the city about registering does not prove you are renting, because the city targets homes not claimed as a homestead. Return a Statement of Exemption for a non-rental home and no fee applies. Even a house where a relative lives rent-free can count as a rental. Community Development is at 1827 N. Squirrel Road, phone 248-364-6900.

Where did Auburn Hills come from?

The city is young on paper and old on the map. It was created in 1983 when Pontiac Township merged with the village of Auburn Heights, though settlement on the Clinton River goes back to 1821, when a sawmill and grist mill drew families to the village of Auburn.

The village faded after the 1860s and was renamed Amy in 1880, then Auburn Heights in 1919. In 1908 automobile pioneer John Dodge bought a farmhouse northeast of the village, and the land he and his wife accumulated grew to 1,400 acres. In 1957 the family donated acreage that became Oakland University. A neighboring country estate, bought by the township in 1975, now serves as the Civic Center.

State officials rejected a 1971 attempt to incorporate as Pontiac Heights. The township became a charter township in 1978 to guard against annexation, and the merger followed five years later. Oakland Community College gave the name Auburn Hills to its campus in 1964, at a former Nike missile base.

Downtown Auburn Hills traces to 2002, when the corner of Auburn and Squirrel roads was revived as the Village Center with new streetscape. By the end of 2013 it had gained a four-story graduate student apartment building, a 233-space parking deck, a University Center for college classes and a restored log cabin that serves as a student and community center. The Seyburn estate that became the Civic Center once had stables, kennels, a swimming pool and a 5,000 square foot Colonial Revival house.

Who employs people in Auburn Hills?

Automotive firms dominate. More than 50 automotive corporations run facilities here, Stellantis keeps its North American headquarters in the city, and the tech and office buildings hold about 80,000 people on a workday.

Other names on the employer list include BorgWarner, PHINIA, Guardian Industries, Autoliv, Joyson Safety Systems, GKN Driveline and Faurecia, plus the North American headquarters of Volkswagen and Audi. Maserati moved its U.S. headquarters into the former Walter P. Chrysler Museum building in 2017. The Oakland Technology Park was approved in 1985, and Great Lakes Crossing Outlets opened on November 12, 1998. The Palace of Auburn Hills, home of the Detroit Pistons, has been demolished.

For residents age 16 and over, 69.9 percent are in the labor force and the mean commute is 22.1 minutes. Those jobs sit a short drive from most houses in the city, and a seller can lean on that in a listing.

Which schools and parks come with an Auburn Hills address?

Three districts serve the city: Avondale, Pontiac and Rochester Community Schools. Avondale runs Graham and Auburn elementary schools inside the city limits, the district offices and a Montessori program, and every Avondale resident is zoned to Avondale High School in Auburn Hills. A Pontiac school, Will Rogers Elementary, sits in the northeast corner. Auburn Hills Christian School and Oakland Christian School are private options.

Buyers also look at parks and trails:

  • The Civic Center Park has nature trails, a fishing pond, a softball field, tennis courts and a nine-hole disc golf course.
  • The free skate park is open from April to November.
  • A 2.1 mile crushed stone stretch of the 16-mile Clinton River Trail crosses the city.

Oakland University and Oakland Community College both have campuses here, and the Auburn Hills Public Library is a local draw.

What does it take to record an Auburn Hills deed in Oakland County?

The Oakland County Register of Deeds records it, and any warranty deed, land contract or deed with a warranty clause needs a stamp from the Oakland County Treasurer first. The office takes calls at 248-858-0597 on weekdays.

State and county transfer taxes together equal $8.60 per $1,000. On a $245,000 sale, the median value in the city, that comes to $2,107, charged to the seller. Because Oakland is a charter county, ask the office for its current recording fee.

Electronic recording works through approved vendors. The county's MiPropDocs tool excludes deeds, which transfer ownership, so a deed goes through a vendor or the office counter.
